Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

(CNN) -- Family members of Phillip Markoff visited him in jail Friday for the first time since his arraignment on murder charges connected to the slaying of a woman he may have met through a Craigslist online ad. The parents, brother and sister-in-law of accused killer Philip Markoff visited him in jail on Friday. Markoff's parents, brother, and sister-in-law visited him Friday, having to get through a throng of media members who gathered near the Boston, Massachusetts, jail. Richard Markoff and Susan Haynes arrived early in the afternoon, CNN affiliate WCVB reported. Markoff's parents stayed at the jail for about two hours and left without making any comments to media, the affiliate reported. Markoff's brother and sister-in-law also visited him on Friday, the affiliate reported. John Salsberg, Markoff's attorney, addressed the crowd of reporters Friday and said he was speaking on behalf of the family. "They love their son very much. They are supportive of him, that's what they would say if they were speaking themselves," he said. It is not yet known if Megan McAllister, Markoff's fiancee, would visit him in jail, but in an e-mail sent to ABC News, she said police have the wrong man and "was set up." "Unfortunately, you were given wrong information as was the public," she wrote. "All I have to say to you is Philip is a beautiful person inside and out and could not hurt a fly!" Markoff, 23, a second-year student at Boston University's School of Medicine, is charged with killing Julissa Brisman, who lived in New York, April 14 at Boston's Copley Marriott Hotel. Police have said Brisman, a model, advertised as a masseuse on Craigslist, a popular online classifieds service. They say Markoff may have met her through the online site. Prosecutors say Brisman sustained blunt head trauma and said the she was shot three times at close range. One of the bullets passed through her heart, killing her, prosecutors said. Markoff is also charged in connection with the April 10 robbery of Trisha Leffler, 29, at a Westin Hotel in Boston, another woman he allegedly met on Craigslist. Leffler was robbed of $800 in cash and $250 in American Express gift cards, police reports said. Prosecutors said she was bound and held at gunpoint. Brisman's mother, Carmen Guzman, released a statement Friday about her devastation. "The feeling of losing my daughter in this way and the pain she must have felt will haunt me for the rest of my life," Guzman said. "She won't live to see her dreams. We will hold Julissa in our hearts every day."

According to prosecutors, Brisman suffered blunt-force trauma to her head and was shot three times from close range. They said one bullet traveled through her heart and caused her death.

Markoff also faces charges related to the April 10 robbery of 29-year-old Trisha Leffler at a Westin Hotel in Boston. Authorities allege that he also met Leffler through Craigslist. Police reports state that $800 in cash and $250 worth of American Express gift cards were taken from her. Prosecutors said she was restrained and threatened with a gun.

On Friday, Brisman’s mother, Carmen Guzman, issued a statement describing her grief. She said she would be haunted for the rest of her life by the way her daughter died and by the pain Julissa must have experienced. Guzman added that her daughter would never have the chance to fulfill her dreams and that her family would remember and cherish her every day.

**BOSTON (CNN)** — Family members of Philip Markoff visited the Boston medical student in jail following his arraignment on charges that he killed a woman he allegedly contacted through Craigslist.

Markoff, 23, was being held without bail at the Nashua Street Jail after pleading not guilty to the murder of Julissa Brisman, a 25-year-old masseuse who was shot at a Boston hotel on April 14, 2009.

Relatives kept a low profile during the visit and did not speak publicly about the case. Markoff’s attorney has maintained that his client is innocent and cautioned against judging him before the evidence is presented in court.

Prosecutors allege Markoff arranged to meet Brisman after she advertised massage services on Craigslist. Authorities say she was bound and shot during an attempted robbery at the Boston Marriott Copley Place.

Markoff also was charged in connection with the armed robbery of another woman who advertised services online. Investigators said similarities between the encounters—including the way the meetings were arranged and the suspect’s behavior—helped lead them to Markoff.

Police arrested Markoff during a traffic stop south of Boston as he traveled with his fiancée. Authorities later searched his apartment in Quincy, Massachusetts, and said they recovered items they believe could be connected to the crimes.

The case drew national attention because of Markoff’s background as a medical student with no widely known criminal history, as well as the alleged use of Craigslist to locate victims.

Markoff remained in custody pending further court proceedings.

## Boston University Medical Student Faced Murder, Robbery Charges in Hotel Attacks

**BOSTON —** Phillip Markoff, a Boston University medical student whose arrest drew national attention, was charged with murdering a woman at a Back Bay hotel and robbing another woman days earlier. Prosecutors alleged that he contacted both victims through advertisements for personal services posted on Craigslist.

Markoff, 23, pleaded not guilty to charges including first-degree murder, armed robbery and kidnapping. He died by suicide in jail in August 2010, before the case could go to trial, leaving the allegations against him unresolved by a jury.

### Killing at the Marriott Copley Place

The murder charge stemmed from the April 14, 2009, death of 25-year-old Julissa Brisman, a New York woman who had advertised massage services online. According to police reports and prosecutors, Brisman arranged to meet a client at the Boston Marriott Copley Place.

Hotel guests reported hearing a commotion and found Brisman injured near the doorway of her room. Authorities said she had been bound or restrained and was shot several times at close range. She was taken to Boston Medical Center, where she was pronounced dead.

Investigators concluded that the encounter began as a robbery. Prosecutors alleged that Brisman resisted her attacker, leading to a struggle and the shooting.

### Earlier robbery at the Westin

Authorities also charged Markoff in connection with an April 10 attack at the nearby Westin Copley Place. In that case, a woman who had advertised escort services told police that a man entered her room, displayed a handgun, bound her with plastic ties and stole money and personal property.

The woman survived and provided investigators with a description. Surveillance recordings from the hotel showed a man whom police later identified as Markoff entering and leaving around the time of the robbery, according to prosecutors and reports by WCVB.

Markoff was separately linked to an April 16 confrontation involving an exotic dancer at a hotel in Warwick, Rhode Island. Authorities there said a man attempted to rob the woman at gunpoint before her husband intervened. That episode became part of the broader investigation into attacks on women who advertised online.

### Digital and surveillance evidence

Prosecutors said the cases were connected through electronic records, hotel-security footage and physical evidence. Investigators traced messages sent to the women’s advertisements and examined internet and telephone records associated with Markoff, according to court presentations and police accounts reported by WCVB.

Markoff was arrested April 20, 2009, while driving south on Interstate 95 with his fiancée, Megan McAllister. Police stopped the couple in Walpole as they were traveling toward Connecticut.

A search of Markoff’s Quincy apartment produced a semiautomatic handgun, ammunition, duct tape and plastic restraints, prosecutors said. Investigators also reported finding items they believed had been taken from victims. Ballistics testing linked the recovered gun to the bullets used in Brisman’s killing, according to the prosecution.

Defense attorneys challenged the government’s case and emphasized that the allegations had not been proved. Markoff maintained his innocence through his not-guilty pleas.

### Families confront conflicting realities

The arrest stunned people close to Markoff, who was then preparing for a career in medicine and planning a wedding. In early public statements, McAllister defended him and said authorities had arrested the wrong person. Members of his family likewise described a version of Markoff sharply at odds with the violent suspect portrayed by prosecutors.

Brisman’s family, meanwhile, mourned a young woman they remembered as loving and energetic. Family statements focused on the pain of her loss and their desire for accountability.

The contrasting reactions became central to public interest in the case: Markoff appeared to be a successful student with no widely known history of serious violence, while police alleged that he had planned a series of armed attacks.

### Death before trial

Markoff remained in custody at Boston’s Nashua Street Jail while awaiting trial. On August 15, 2010, authorities found him dead in his cell. Officials ruled the death a suicide.

Because Markoff died before trial, the criminal proceedings ended without a verdict and the charges were dismissed as a matter of law. Brisman’s relatives said his death deprived them of the opportunity to see the evidence tested in court and to obtain the formal resolution they had sought.

The case nevertheless became one of the most prominent early examples of investigators using online communications and digital records to connect a suspect to crimes arranged through classified-advertising websites.

**CORRESPONDENT PACKAGE**

BOSTON — Philip Markoff’s parents, his brother and his sister-in-law arrived at the Suffolk County Jail on Nashua Street to visit the former Boston University medical student, who was being held without bail on murder and armed-robbery charges.

The family members avoided extended comments as they entered and left the facility. Their visit nevertheless offered a visible sign of support for Markoff as investigators examined his alleged connection to attacks on women who advertised services online.

Prosecutors also alleged that Markoff robbed another woman at gunpoint at the Westin Copley Place several days earlier. He pleaded not guilty.

Markoff’s attorney, John Salsberg, cautioned against assuming his client’s guilt based on police statements, leaked evidence or widespread news coverage. Salsberg said Markoff had a supportive family and emphasized that prosecutors would be required to prove every allegation beyond a reasonable doubt. He also raised concerns that the enormous publicity surrounding the case could make it difficult to select an impartial jury.

Markoff’s fiancée, Megan McAllister, likewise publicly defended him in the period following his arrest. McAllister said the man described by investigators was not the person she knew and indicated that she believed in his innocence. The couple had been planning a wedding, but those plans were thrown into uncertainty by the criminal case.

For Brisman’s family, however, the focus remained on the young woman who lost her life.

Brisman’s mother, Carmen Guzman, described her daughter as loving and hardworking and spoke of the devastation caused by her death. She said she wanted the person responsible held fully accountable and expressed anguish that her daughter’s final moments had been violent and terrifying.

Police alleged that electronic records, surveillance images and other evidence connected Markoff to the hotel encounters. Investigators also searched locations associated with him and said they recovered items they considered relevant to the case. Defense attorneys warned that individual pieces of evidence could be misleading when presented without context.

The family visit came as Markoff remained under close supervision at the Boston jail. Officials disclosed few details about the private meeting, and his relatives did not offer a substantive public response to the charges.

**CORRESPONDENT TAG**

Markoff was presumed innocent unless and until convicted. His attorney said the defense would challenge the prosecution’s evidence, while Brisman’s family said it would continue pressing for justice as the case moved through the Massachusetts courts.
